desk.headline: Revenue up 0.5% to $17.3bn; adjusted EPS $9.76, well above $7.03 estimate despite higher storm losses; no outlook given
results: Adjusted EPS fell 13% to $9.76 as catastrophe losses tripled to $1.65bn, but was still far above the $7.03 estimate; GAAP EPS was $8.03.
Property-Liability earned premiums grew 3.8% to $15.1bn; the combined ratio rose to 86.6 from 80.1, helped by 5.1 points of reserve releases.
Auto stayed profitable (combined ratio 83.2) but the underlying ratio rose to 89.8 on lower average premiums; auto policies grew 3.4%.
Net investment income rose $228m to $1.18bn, but investment losses of $545m came as interest rates rose.
About $1.5bn went back to shareholders through buybacks and dividends; $1.3bn remains on the $4.0bn buyback plan.

guidance.summary: Allstate does not give earnings guidance, and none was given with these results.

points: Management acknowledged auto margin pressure from lower average premiums and rising claims costs, but said margins beat its target.
Reserve releases came mostly from better handling of injury claims; management said further releases should not be assumed.
New business grew 6.3% in auto and 10.2% in homeowners, credited to more advertising, wider distribution and new products.
Allstate plans a personal digital assistant for customers in early 2027, built on its in-house ALLIE system, and is engaging regulators.
Allstate's own sales offices will choose one of three new operating models during 2027, taking effect on 1 January 2028.
call.source: Call coverage: Zacks via Yahoo Finance, 6 Nov 2026 (Exhibit 99.2 is a data supplement, not prepared remarks)

watch: Auto underlying combined ratio as average premiums fall and claims costs rise.
Q4 catastrophe losses and whether reserve releases continue.
Pace of buybacks with $1.3bn left on the authorisation.
